change.summary: HTTP Basic authentication with an account password was removed across every endpoint; such requests began returning 401. Personal access tokens, OAuth tokens or GitHub App tokens were required instead.
change.replacement: username + personal access token via Basic auth, or an OAuth/App token

spec.note: The spec repo existed from 2020-06-22, about five months before the cutoff, so it was watchable — and still could not have helped. GitHub's OpenAPI description has no components.securitySchemes and no top-level security key at all, so authentication is simply not modelled. This class of change cannot produce a spec diff even in principle.

changelog.note: 374 days of lead time — but only for someone watching developer.github.com. The github.blog changelog entry was published 2020-11-13T17:01Z, roughly an hour AFTER the 16:00Z cutoff, giving zero lead time to anyone monitoring the more obvious feed. The site carrying the real warning has since been frozen.

contract.note: GitHub ran two deliberate brownouts (2020-09-30 and 2020-10-28, three-hour blocks) explicitly so that callers' own alerting would fire. A live contract check during a brownout window would have failed, giving 44 days of warning — a provider deliberately creating a signal for exactly this kind of verification.

notes: Close to a best-case provider process — 374 days' notice, two brownouts, and targeted emails naming the offending endpoint and user agent — and people still broke. Worth remembering when judging what better tooling can realistically achieve. The Teams API endpoint move was considered instead and rejected: its sunset was paused after the first brownout, so it has no clean effective date, though it would make a good false-alarm case later.
